name: agent-bridge-concurrent-daemon
description: Tier-P F1 single-instance daemon-guard scenario: install + provision agent-bridge on a fresh box, then drive the REAL single-instance guard (agent_bridge.singleton.SingleInstance over the shared single_instance_lease OS byte-range lock) under concurrent start and assert the guard that prevents the duplicate-daemon failure mode at its root -- when a second daemon races the first (the classic case is a concurrent sessionStart-hook reinstall spawning a second daemon while one is live), the guard must REFUSE the duplicate instead of standing a colliding daemon up beside it. Complements agent-bridge-concurrent-relay (which proves the relay recovers if a duplicate slips through); this one proves the duplicate is refused before it can bind at all. Checks: (duplicate-refused) a live holder owns the lease for a config dir + port, a second acquire raises AlreadyRunningError naming the holder pid; (dead-holder-reclaimed) a holder acquires then is KILLED, a fresh acquire SUCCEEDS -- the OS frees the lock on death so a stale lock never wedges startup; (passive-coexist-by-port) a holder on port A + a second instance on the SAME config dir but port B coexist (active/passive cutover keys on the port). FIDELITY: a fully live 'two installed daemons race the installer end-to-end' assertion is a Tier-E concern; this Tier-P probe proves the guard MECHANISM. The probe is portable stdlib-only (drives the real guard with cross-process holders), so it is verifiable off-Docker too. Name-free / public.

stages.title: single-instance daemon guard under concurrent start
